title: Mobile App Development Readiness
description: Assess your skills in mobile UI layouts, React Native/Flutter, offline caching, lifecycle methods, and native device APIs.

questions.question: In React Native, which component should be used to render large, scrollable lists with high performance and memory virtualization?
options: <ScrollView>
<FlatList>
<View>
<ListView>
questions.explanation: FlatList only renders items currently visible on screen (windowing), saving memory and ensuring smooth 60fps scrolling.

questions.question: In mobile layout engines (Flexbox in React Native), what is the default `flexDirection`?
options: row
column
row-reverse
column-reverse
questions.explanation: Unlike web CSS where flexDirection defaults to 'row', React Native defaults to 'column' to match portrait mobile screens.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between asynchronous storage (AsyncStorage/MMKV) and SQLite in mobile apps?
options: AsyncStorage is key-value for small data; SQLite is a relational database for structured queries
SQLite only works on Android
AsyncStorage requires a continuous internet connection
SQLite cannot store numbers
questions.explanation: AsyncStorage/MMKV is designed for key-value preferences and tokens, while SQLite handles relational tables and complex queries.

questions.question: Which native operating system capability handles background push notifications when an app is closed on iOS and Android?
options: Apple APNs (Apple Push Notification service) and Google FCM (Firebase Cloud Messaging)
WebSockets running in the foreground
Local HTTP long-polling
Bluetooth Low Energy broadcasting
questions.explanation: APNs (iOS) and FCM (Android) are OS-level push services that wake up apps and deliver notifications even when closed.

questions.question: In mobile navigation, what is a 'Stack Navigator'?
options: A navigation pattern where new screens are pushed on top of a stack and popped when going back
A horizontal tab bar at the bottom of the screen
A hidden side menu that slides in from the left
A modal dialog for entering passwords
questions.explanation: Stack navigation transitions between screens by pushing new routes onto a navigation history stack.

questions.question: What causes UI frame drops and sluggish animations on mobile devices?
options: Heavy synchronous JavaScript computations running on the main UI JavaScript thread
Using PNG images instead of JPEG
Having more than 3 screens in navigation
Using dark mode styling
questions.explanation: When the JS thread is blocked with heavy computations, animation frames are dropped, causing lag. Using native animation drivers prevents this.

questions.question: In Swift (iOS development), what is an 'Optional'?
options: A type that can hold either a concrete value or `nil` (absence of value)
A function that executes only if battery is > 50%
A button that the user can skip pressing
A framework that can be removed from the build
questions.explanation: Optionals in Swift represent values that may or may not exist, safely preventing null pointer exceptions at runtime.

questions.question: In Kotlin (Android development), what are Coroutines primarily used for?
options: Managing asynchronous, non-blocking background operations smoothly without callback hell
Rendering vector XML drawables
Defining Android Manifest permissions
Creating custom hardware drivers
questions.explanation: Kotlin coroutines provide lightweight concurrency for network calls, database queries, and async background tasks.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Safe Area in modern mobile app UI design?
options: Ensuring UI elements are not obscured by device notches, camera cutouts, or home indicator bars
Encrypting sensitive user passwords on screen
Limiting app download size in app stores
Preventing accidental screen taps by children
questions.explanation: SafeArea insets pad content so it does not overlap status bars, camera islands, rounded display corners, or home swipe indicators.

questions.question: What is 'CodePush' or Over-The-Air (OTA) update in React Native apps?
options: Deploying JavaScript and asset bundle fixes directly to user devices without submitting a new binary build to App Stores
Pushing code from GitHub directly to Android Studio
Updating device firmware automatically
Testing code on physical devices over Wi-Fi
questions.explanation: OTA updates allow developers to publish urgent JS bundle and asset bug fixes directly to end users instantly without full App Store review.
